scope: Controlled synthetic temporal software testing; no clinical guidance or inference
source: Human-authored abstract behavioral requirements, not compiler-produced MR specifications

requirements.requirement: Changing a reporting timestamp while holding the specimen time and value fixed must not change a decision when both versions are available by the decision point.
An explicitly redundant nonanchor measurement may be removed without changing a minimum-based summary.
A decision determined only by protected clinical state should not be affected by an auxiliary nonstate attribute.
Removing an intermediate nonanchor measurement must preserve the protected anchors and not reduce the ordinal risk level in the synthetic reference policy.
A bounded increasing slope perturbation of noninitial measurements must not decrease a declared ordinal risk outcome.
A transient additional low observation followed by recovery should not change a decision defined solely by the original initial measurement.
Shifting only the effective time of one observation by a configured seven days must preserve a time-independent numeric decision.
Conversion between an explicitly supported unit pair must preserve the canonical numeric magnitude.
